audit_notes: Model: steady 1D series conduction interior -> wall -> cork board -> white mineral skin with sol-air Robin boundary; q = [alpha*I + h*dT - eps*R_net]/(1 + h*R_tot). Checks: expanded cork board k = 0.040 W/mK (0.037-0.045 typical), 40 mm -> R = 1.0 m2K/W; aged SR 0.72 for a white silicate render is plausible (slightly better than acrylic at 0.67, because mineral renders are less thermoplastic and pick up less dirt). Facade conditions I = 180 W/m2, R_net = 40 W/m2 are appropriate for a west facade. Hand solution: design (50.4 + 150 - 36)/(1 + 45) = 3.57 W/m2; baseline (SR 0.67 directly on the wall) (59.4 + 150 - 36)/31 = 5.59 W/m2; gain ~36 %. About 33 of the 36 points come from the added 1.0 m2K/W, which any ETICS with 40 mm mineral wool gives; the skin contributes ~3 points. Structural: cork boards are dimensionally stable, rot-resistant and have been used as exposed facades for decades; a thin mineral skin on cork needs a reinforcing mesh, otherwise it cracks at board joints; cork creeps little. Fire: cork is combustible (Euroclass E), which restricts use on taller buildings. Simulation coefficient: effective conductance 1/(R_tot + 1/h) = 0.33 W/m2K.
